claim: Bayes's goal update is the new observation's likelihood averaged over the contextual variable with the current belief pi_{t-1}(k|j) (telescoping identity); naive Bayes uses uniform weights per observable, the step-wise rule per step, block/window rules in between. Every rule beyond naive differs from naive only in how far back that belief reaches.
verification: algebra (Appendix A); the identity was checked numerically to 5e-14 in v2_bayes_parts.json; the rules derived from it reproduce the stored ladder exactly (see reference_ladder).

claim: Every logit table is rank one, x_i(j,k;z) = u_i(j;z) v_i(k;z).
verification: the generator builds x as a product of two soft_roll profiles; recomputed singular values.

claim: For any update theta_dot = -P grad L with P >= 0, the logits obey Y_dot = -K G with K = J P J^T (reach) and G = dL/dY (push); frozen stages contribute nothing to K; for a linear read-out on fixed features the reach is exactly the feature span.
verification: chain rule (Appendix A).

claim: On a state affine in the counts, a linear marginal read-out gives goal contrasts affine in the counts (zero interaction between observations); with per-observable loadings it is naive Bayes's family.
episode_set: within-environment variance of the summed state, stored checkpoints
verification: proof in Appendix A; the affine shares are read from the compact note (forward passes), not recomputed here.

claim: On the same state a linear joint read-out followed by row sums gives LSE_k of affine functions of the counts: Bayes's form, with Bayes a member. The row sum equals LSE_k Y(j,k) minus a constant.
verification: proof in Appendix A; the row-sum identity checked numerically.

claim: An output that is a sum over steps of functions of w-step windows has zero interaction between observations w or more steps apart and, if it depends only on the counts, is affine in them; a frozen stage responding linearly to its input, read out linearly and summed, is such a sum with w = 1 whatever its memory.
verification: short proof in Appendix A; the L2 bounds of the full theorem are cited, not re-proved.

claim: For any loss depending on joint logits through the row log-masses, dL/dY(j,k) = q(k|j) dL/dm(j) (Fisher's identity): the goal-loss gradient is the joint-loss gradient with the network's own conditional in place of Bayes's; it is the softmax policy gradient with the cells as actions; recovery from depth u0 needs time >= (e^{u0}-1)/C. A marginal output is not gated.
verification: proof in Appendix A; autograd check.

claim: The joint loss gives G = q - p*, which does not vanish for unlikely cells, and a convex read-out problem; an entropy bonus pushes cell r by beta q(r)[log(1/q(r)) - H], a gate that closes more slowly than q.
verification: proof in Appendix A.

claim: A network learns beyond naive Bayes only along directions that are in its reach and receive a push; the contextual belief enters the reach only through trained nonlinear processing after the combination of evidence or through the joint output's LSE, and is pushed ungated through a marginal output but gated by the network's own belief through a joint output. Necessity follows from P2-P4; sufficiency is measured (Table 1).
verification: the necessity is the conjunction of P2, P3 and P4; every row of Table 1 is consistent with it; no counterexample was found (Appendix D).
